newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Amcor says to grow profits from assets.
newsitem.headline: Amcor says to grow profits from assets.

text.p: Paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd said on Wednesday it expected profit growth to come from existing assets, as the group consolidated current businesses following a big expansion in the first half of the 1990s.
"We will have to grow profits from our existing asset base," managing director Don Macfarlane told a Securities Institute of Australia luncheon.

Amcor spent A$3 billion on acquisitions and capital expenditure in the three years to 1996. Macfarlane said he expected the group to spend A$500 million on capital expenditure in each of the years to June 30, 1997 and 1997/98.

Last week, Amcor announced it expected profit for the second half ending June 30, 1997, to be lower than the year ago period and lower than the 1996/97 first half. It also said it expected significant writedowns in some assets in the 1996/97 year.

However, Macfarlane said the expected lower 1996/97 profit did not mean the company would be cutting its final dividend for the six months ended June 30. Amcor paid 20 cents a share dividend in the 1995/96 second half.
Macfarlane said the group planned to improve profitability through cost cutting and had no plans for major acquisitions.
Marfarlane said the company planned further plant closures as part of its cost cutting programme.
"We have aleady closed about 20 plants in Australia and New Zealand so far and we plan to close or merge another 10 plants in Australia and New Zealand," Macfarlane said.

He said Amcor planned to grow profits from cost cutting, new products and on the company's ability to develop new technological solutions for packaging businesses and the growth of its customers businesses in Australia and in export markets. Amcor planned to build two new corrugated box plants in Australia using a new box making technology called XITEX.
Marfarlane said the cost of the new plants would be about A$13 million.
A spokesman for Amcor said the group aimed to make a margin of between 18 and 20 percent on earnings before tax and interest on funds employed.
Amcor reported a 34.1 percent fall in net profit to A$140.6 million in the six months ended December 31, 1996.
At 3.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), Amcor shares were four cents down at A$8.38.
